commits.edited_message:
liblzma: Make lzma_lz_decoder_init() safe to reinit after alloc failure

Allocate the new dictionary before freeing the old one so that a failed
allocation leaves the old dictionary buffer intact and there is no NULL
or dangling pointer in coder->dict.buf. The new dictionary size is
stored also when the allocation fails, so a reinit attempt with the same
dictionary size will not repeat an allocation that is known to fail.

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

Filter coders are initialized using lzma_next_filter_init(). If filter
chain initialization fails, the entire filter chain should be cleaned up
with lzma_next_end(). lzma_raw_encoder_init() and lzma_raw_decoder_init()
have always done this via lzma_raw_coder_init() in filter_common.c.
(Separate cleanup is weird, but it must have made sense to the young me.)

The following decoders initialize the LZMA1 filter directly without using
the raw filter chain API. This avoids needlessly pulling in all other filters
when a program is linked against static liblzma. These functions didn't
call lzma_next_end() after an initialization error, which left the state
available for later reinitialization.

  - lzma_alone_decoder()
  - lzma_lzip_decoder()
  - lzma_auto_decoder() [*]
  - lzma_microlzma_decoder()

[*] lzma_auto_decoder() is only indirectly affected due to the first two
    functions. lzma_auto_decoder() itself doesn't need a fix.

In lzma_alone_decoder(), LZMA_MEM_ERROR from the sub-coder initialization
is excluded from the cleanup: the LZMA decoder keeps its earlier state
when an allocation fails and the application is allowed to retry after
more memory becomes available.

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect is a heap-buffer-overflow write in the LZ decoder dictionary and it is born only from the composition of the two edited commits; neither edit contains a reachable violation on its own.

EDIT A (62ed2b0, src/liblzma/lz/lz_decoder.c) rewrites the dictionary reallocation in lzma_lz_decoder_init() to allocate before freeing, and on allocation failure it stores the NEW alloc_size into coder->dict.size while deliberately keeping the OLD (smaller) dictionary buffer valid. Each piece looks like reasonable hardening: no dangling/NULL pointer, and a same-size reinit skips an allocation known to fail.

EDIT B (6cd45fb, src/liblzma/common/alone_decoder.c) exempts LZMA_MEM_ERROR from the lzma_next_end() cleanup that this same commit introduces for filter-chain initialization failures, on the rationale that an allocation failure leaves the sub-coder reusable for a later retry.

Why the bug needs both: after EDIT A alone fails an 8 MiB dictionary allocation, the lz_coder holds (old 4704-byte buffer, dict.size = 8 MiB) - an inconsistent state - but the real 6cd45fb destroys that lz_coder with lzma_next_end() on every init error, so the marked state is unreachable by any decode (verified: PoC is clean on the EDIT-A-only tree). With EDIT B alone, the kept coder comes from the real 62ed2b0 failure path whose state is (NULL, 0), which forces a fresh allocation attempt on reinit and can never overrun (verified: PoC is clean on the EDIT-B-only tree). Only when both edits are present does the kept-alive coder carry the marked size: a retry of the SAME .lzma header makes coder->dict.size == alloc_size true, the allocation block is skipped entirely, and decoding proceeds with dict.limit computed from the 8 MiB size while dict.buf is still the 4704-byte buffer. The LZMA literal decoder then writes past the end of the small buffer in dict_put() (heap-buffer-overflow WRITE, ASan aborts).

Why a correct fix is non-local: the reviewer must see that the two commits share one invariant - what a failed dictionary allocation leaves behind, and who is allowed to consume it. Commit A's comment claims the old buffer stays 'intact and reusable', which is only harmless if every consumer of a marked-but-smaller dictionary is destroyed on error; commit B's comment claims an allocation failure leaves the sub-coder 'reusable', which is only true if the sub-coder's state is self-consistent. Each comment is false exactly in the other commit's presence. Restoring either the unconditional lzma_next_end() (commit B) or the failure-path size reset/NULLing (commit A) removes the overflow, so fixing either single diff alone already repairs the tree - the defect is attributable to neither diff alone, only to their composition. Notably, the project's own regression test for this scenario (tests/test_alone_decoder.c, added in the batch) still passes on the edited tree because it retries with a different dictionary size; only a same-size retry after a failed allocation exposes the bug.

pocs.entry_point: liblzma public API: lzma_alone_encoder/lzma_lzma_preset to build a valid 8 KiB .lzma file, then lzma_alone_decoder + lzma_code + lzma_end on a single reused lzma_stream with a custom lzma_allocator that rejects allocations >= 1 MiB (API-contract allocator failure injection)
